# Replay vectors for the port of Tencent TQUIC's delivery_rate.rs.
#
# Generated by running the UPSTREAM file, verbatim, at TQUIC commit
# 938e90adb460b5ff08b2bc6d11a3e1ba52c27a8d (src/congestion_control/delivery_rate.rs),
# in a standalone harness that compiled only that file against stub
# SentPacket / RateSamplePacketState types. The trace is a scripted
# bottleneck: saturated phases (ack every 1, 2, 3 packets, 0-4 % loss, a
# capacity change, small ack reordering) and sparse app-limited phases with
# duplicate acknowledgements.
#
# Lines:  S <t_us> <pkt> <size> <bytes_in_flight> <bytes_lost>   packet sent
#         L <0|1>                                               set_app_limited
#         A <t_us> <pkt,pkt,..>                                  acknowledgement
#         R <delivery_rate> <delivered> <sample_delivered>
#           <sample_prior_delivered> <sample_app_limited> <sample_rtt_us>
#                                         upstream's reading after the A above
#
# To regenerate (from the repository root; the harness is tools/tquic-delivery-rate-vectors,
# a standalone crate outside the workspace):
#   D=tools/tquic-delivery-rate-vectors; S=$(mktemp -d)
#   curl -sSL -o $D/src/delivery_rate.rs \
#     https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tencent/tquic/938e90adb460b5ff08b2bc6d11a3e1ba52c27a8d/src/congestion_control/delivery_rate.rs
#   python3 $D/gen_trace.py > $S/trace_in.txt
#   cargo run --release --manifest-path $D/Cargo.toml -- $S/trace_in.txt > $S/trace_out.txt
#   { grep '^#' <this file>; cat $S/trace_out.txt; } > <this file>.new   # keep this header
# The result is byte-identical to the body below (checked when this recipe was written).
